To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ingestion of MPs and MFs was a widespread phenomenon in the Adriatic Sea with higher values in the Central and Southern basing compared to the Northern basin, as well as for benthopelagics compared to benthics and pelagics; (2) ingestion of MFs was more frequent than MPs; (3) the frequency of ingestion appeared a more reliable parameter than the number of particles to compare different areas or species.
the ingestion of plastic particles in the Adriatic food webs is a widespread phenomenon and that it is influenced by geographical areas and ecological features of the organisms.
Microplastics and textile microfibres (MFs) are widespread in the Adriatic Sea food webs and their ingestion by organisms is a widespread phenomenon, especially for MFs.

the characterization of microplastics and microfibers in the Adriatic Sea.
the characterization of microplastics and textile microfibres in Adriatic food web and the development of a common biomointoring strategy for the Mediterranean area.

the need to improve the knowledge on the occurrence of microplastics and microfibers, in order to understand their potential impact on food web dynamics, as well as on the health of marine ecosystems.

, in the Adriatic Sea food webs, MPs and MFs are ubiquitous and widespread, but their ingestion frequency, number and typology of particles are species and area dependent.
the ingestion of microplastics by marine organisms is widespread, but the frequency of ingestion is a better indicator than the number of microplastics ingested.

microplastics and MFs are ubiquitous in the marine environment and in the food web of the Adriatic Sea and, therefore, the need for further research on their fate and effects in the Mediterranean Sea is evident and urgent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ingestion of microplastics is a widespread phenomenon, with the frequency of occurrence being the most reliable index to highlight differences in the exposure of different species and trophic levels.

the frequency of ingestion and the typology of microplastics (natural, semi-synthetic, synthetic) are more reliable indices for the evaluation of the impact of microplastics than the number of microplastics ingested.
the Adriatic Sea is a hotspot for plastic pollution and microplastic ingestion in marine biota.

microplastic ingestion is widespread in Adriatic food web and that a multi-species and multi-trophic approach should be considered for biomonitoring studies.
